# Thrum v0.11.0-dev

> Git-backed messaging for AI agent coordination. Real-time. Cross-machine. Cross-repo. Persistent.

## What is Thrum

Thrum is a messaging and coordination system for AI agents. Messages are stored
in append-only JSONL logs (sharded by agent) on a dedicated `a-sync` orphan
branch, accessed via a `.git/thrum-sync/a-sync` git worktree. A SQLite projection provides
fast queries. A background daemon provides JSON-RPC over Unix socket and
WebSocket, with automatic Git sync every 60 seconds. No branch switching is
needed -- all sync operations happen within the worktree.

New in v0.7.0: single-agent mode (default for new repos), cross-repo peer
communication via Tailscale, PID-based identity resolution, and a three-tier
context model for session persistence across compaction.

New in v0.7.1: tmux-managed sessions replace background listeners with instant
daemon-driven nudge delivery. Session restart extracts conversation history from
JSONL transcripts and reloads it in new sessions.

New in v0.8.0:
- Tmux command queue (`thrum tmux queue/queue-status/cancel`) — daemon-managed
  FIFO dispatch with `@system` completion notifications and restart recovery.
- Worktree management (`thrum worktree create/teardown/list`) — git worktrees
  with automatic thrum and beads redirect wiring.
- Orchestrator role — plan execution with review gates, agent lifecycle, and
  worktree management. Includes `thrum:orchestrate` skill.
- Multi-runtime tmux — `ClaudePID` renamed to `AgentPID` (schema v17).
  `PreferredRuntime` field + `--runtime` flag on `thrum quickstart`. OpenCode,
  Codex, and other runtimes launch via tmux alongside Claude.
- Agent status (`thrum agent set-status working|idle|blocked`) — auto-nudge
  detection when working status mismatches silent pane.
- Daemon logging — slog + lumberjack rotation. `thrum daemon logs` command.
  Configurable `daemon.log_level` in config.json.
- Graceful restart flow — `thrum tmux restart` (without `--force`) asks the
  agent to save its own snapshot before killing, falling back to JSONL
  extraction on timeout.

New in v0.8.1: CI fix for npm publish packaging (no user-facing changes).

New in v0.8.2:
- Cursor plugin — full Cursor integration with rules, hooks, skills, commands,
  and MCP config. Deployed via `cursor-plugin/local-install.sh` into `.cursor/`.
- Antigravity (agy) — converts the Claude Code plugin: `agy plugin install
  https://github.com/leonletto/thrum-pro/tree/main/claude-plugin`. No hooks or MCP
  after conversion; Thrum types `/thrum:prime`.
- Worktree create quickstart fix — `thrum worktree create` with quickstart
  flags now creates a real tmux session (kept, not destroyed) and runs
  quickstart inside it via SendKeys instead of the old temp-session + queue
  RPC path that rejected agentless sessions. Daemon-side retry at 5s if shell
  init swallowed the command, CLI-side pane capture at 12s if the identity
  file still hasn't appeared. Repo-root guard: errors out if the resolved
  worktree path or `worktrees.base_path` is the repo root itself.
- Two-step create + launch — `thrum worktree create` and `thrum tmux create`
  now print explicit next-step hints: "Agent is NOT running yet. Start it
  with: thrum tmux launch <name>". The agent identity is registered, but the
  runtime is not started until `tmux launch` runs.
- `thrum tmux launch` hard-errors on missing identity — sessions created
  with `--no-agent` (or worktrees with no identity file) cannot be launched.
  Returns an error telling you to run `thrum quickstart` first. Launching a
  runtime without an identity is a no-op.
- Next-step guard messages — `agent register`, `worktree create` (no agent),
  `purge --confirm`, `daemon stop`, and `tmux restart` now print explicit
  hints about what to do next or what just broke. `daemon stop` warns that
  messaging commands will fail until the daemon is restarted. `tmux restart`
  warns when the snapshot has 0 lines (no conversation history).
- Purge auto-re-register message corrected — agents auto-re-register via
  `RefreshLocalIdentity` wired into `getClient()`, so no manual action is
  needed after `thrum purge`.

New in v0.9.0:
- Safe agent registration — `thrum tmux create` now requires quickstart flags
  (`--name`, `--role`, `--module`) or `--no-agent`; runs quickstart inside the
  pane automatically. New alias: `thrum tmux quickstart`.
  `thrum worktree create` gains optional quickstart flags; when all three are
  provided it creates a real tmux session and runs quickstart inside it.
  New alias: `thrum worktree setup`. Single-identity-per-worktree enforcement.
- Monitor Jobs — `thrum monitor start/list/show/update/stop/delete/logs/restart`.
  Spawn a child process, watch stdout+stderr with a regex, and emit matches as
  synthetic Thrum messages to a target agent. (`thrum monitor add` is an alias
  for `thrum monitor start`.) Leading-edge debounce (default 60s).
  Local-only, max 100 monitors. `stop` leaves the record behind and reserves
  the name — `delete` is what frees it for reuse.
- Permission prompt detection — daemon-side silence-hash poller (~20s detection
  latency). Polls every 10s; stable on 2 identical hashes. Permission nudges
  auto-forward to Telegram when bridge is configured and bridge user is a
  `permission_supervisors` entry. Reply via threaded reply (y/yes/approve/a or
  n/no/deny/d) OR fresh DM (y/n/yes/no/allow/deny — note `approve` and `a`
  don't trigger fresh-DM path).
- Identity guards — 8 named enforcement checkpoints (cross_worktree, G1a/G1b
  quickstart guards, non_git_bootstrap, unauthenticated_rpc,
  daemon_writer_liveness, prime_ownership, dead_pid_auto_reclaim).
  3 modes: strict / warn / off.
- Schema v24 (permission_nudges v21, origin_daemon col v22, daemon_identity v23,
  telegram_msg_map v24).
- CLI hints (Phase B/D) — contextual hints wired on `thrum init`, `thrum send`,
  `thrum tmux create`, `thrum team` (and more). Two kinds: `detection`
  (condition-triggered guards; fires when condition present) and `reinforcement`
  (periodic memory-aids, band-throttled by context-%). Shape B = stderr trailer
  `  <severity> [<code>]: <message>`; Shape C = JSON top-level `"hints"` array
  with fields: code, severity, message, options[], kind. kind always present.
  Suppress: --quiet or THRUM_NO_HINTS=1 drops all; THRUM_NO_REMINDERS=1 drops
  reinforcement only (both stderr and JSON); --json moves hints into JSON body.
  Phase D: daemon RPC responses can carry hints[] merged into top-level; AP-4
  `daemon.cross-version-drift` WARN detection hint on `thrum team` (peer version
  mismatch).
- Peer drift reconciliation — `peer join --type repair` for in-place re-pairing
  without new peercode. `drift_reconcile_failed` shown as inline hint in peer list.
- Permission supervisors — configure via `permission_supervisors` config key
  (array of role/agent/user names; default ["coordinator"]) and `project_name`
  (owner of @supervisor_<project> pseudo-agent). Detection: daemon-side
  SessionPoller; pattern match + stability hash scoped to bottom 15 lines of
  pane capture. Claude deny key is per-shape via DisambiguateClaudeDeny:
  "3" (3-option Variant A), "2" (2-option Variant B-Bash, option 2 starts with
  "No"), "Escape" (2-option Variant B-Read / unknown). Snippet truncation is
  tail-biased (last 5-6 lines) with ANSI strip.
- BREAKING: `peer add --type` and `peer join --type` now MANDATORY.

New in v0.9.1:
- Peercred resolver error taxonomy — introspection failures at
  Step 1 (kernel peer credentials) and Step 2 (gopsutil CWD) no longer wrap
  `ErrAnonymous`. They return raw errors so the server falls through to the
  legacy client-asserted identity path (pre-v0.9.0 behavior). Only Step 3
  (no git root above CWD) and Step 5 (CWD's git root doesn't match any
  registered worktree) are PROVABLY anonymous — those still wrap
  `ErrAnonymous` and trigger the allowlist-rejection error
  `anonymous caller cannot invoke "<method>": cd into a registered agent
  worktree and retry`.
  Diagnostic path: slog.Warn fires at both introspection-failure paths with
  `step=pid failed` (kernel peercred) or `step=cwd failed` (gopsutil). Grep
  daemon logs for those keys to distinguish "we couldn't classify you" from
  "you are provably outside every registered worktree".
  Fixes 2026-04-24 breakage where claude-code Bash subprocesses on macOS hit
  gopsutil.Cwd races (subprocess exits before introspection completes) and
  interactive zsh callers hit the same path — both were incorrectly rejected
  as anonymous despite being legitimate callers.
- thrum setup claude-md --apply (issue #8) — implemented the
  documented-but-missing CLI subcommand. External users following the
  quickstart hit `Error: unknown flag: --apply` because the setupCmd stub
  only suggested `thrum worktree setup`. The command now installs a
  Thrum-managed block (wrapped in `<!-- BEGIN THRUM -->...<!-- END THRUM -->`
  markers) into ./CLAUDE.md. Three forms: bare prints to stdout, --apply
  creates-or-appends, --apply --force replaces existing block idempotently.
  Errors with exit 1 if a block exists and --force is not set. Template is
  static (go:embed) and intentionally minimal (~30-40 lines: what Thrum
  is, 5 essential commands, docs pointer). Plugin-vs-standalone framing:
  use this path ONLY when not running the Claude Code Thrum plugin —
  the plugin already injects messaging instructions, so combining the two
  duplicates content. The CLAUDE.md block is the alternative for other
  runtimes (codex, cursor, opencode) and for Claude Code
  without the plugin.

New in v0.10.1:
- Hotfix for v0.10.0 quickstart-redirect regression. `thrum quickstart`
  from a worktree using `.thrum/redirect` was writing the agent's
  identity file to `$THRUM_HOME/.thrum/identities/` instead of the
  caller's worktree, with `worktree` field also set to `$THRUM_HOME`.
  Latent bug since March; surfaced because the
  wizard + worktree-create flow routes through `buildInlineQuickstartCmd`
  more often, which sends `thrum quickstart` into daemon-spawned panes
  that inherit `THRUM_HOME` from the daemon. Fix: PersistentPreRunE
  exempts `init` and `quickstart` from `THRUM_HOME` substitution;
  `BuildQuickstartCmd` now accepts and emits `--repo <path>` explicitly
  on the daemon-inline path; `quickstart`'s G1a/G1b guard and Step 2.5
  enrichment paths drop redundant `EffectiveRepoPath` calls.
  Regression tests cover local and remote quickstart. v0.10.0 is marked prerelease; upgrade to v0.10.1.
- Boot-time identity reconcile. Write RPCs (`thrum send`, `thrum tmux
  start`) from a registered worktree no longer fail with `anonymous
  caller cannot invoke X` after a daemon restart. The peercred
  resolver matches caller CWDs against `session_refs JOIN sessions
  WHERE ended_at IS NULL`; that view is durable in SQLite but loses
  rows on shutdown / cleanup / long quiescence, so disk truth (identity
  files) and resolver truth (DB rows) drifted apart. Previously only
  `thrum quickstart --force` repopulated; `thrum prime` did not. The
  daemon walks
  `.thrum/identities/*.json` at boot and inserts the missing
  `(sessions, session_refs)` pairs through `safedb` in a per-identity
  transaction with `INSERT OR IGNORE`. Local-only — direct SQL, no
  JSONL events, no cross-machine sync. Same pass also restores the
  in-memory `sessionCwds` pane-nudge map for live tmux sessions.
  A defensive guard skips fixture stub files, and the pass is bounded to 10s.

New in v0.10.0:
- `thrum init` interactive wizard — on a TTY, `thrum init` now launches a
  multi-step wizard (identity → worktrees-root → role-template → daemon).
  Press enter through every prompt to accept defaults. Legacy silent path
  is preserved on non-TTY stdin or with `--non-interactive`. Pre-fill any
  prompt with `--name`, `--role`, `--module`, `--worktrees-root`,
  `--roles=enhanced|default|skip`, `--no-daemon`. `--force` re-init
  pre-seeds prompts from existing `.thrum/config.json` and identity.
  Transactional: SIGINT or step-failure restores `.gitignore` and
  `.git/info/exclude` byte-for-byte.
- New role template `implementer-worktree-write-only.md` — wizard's
  "enhanced" choice ships an implementer preamble that pins writes to the
  agent's own worktree and forbids drive-by edits to the main repo.
- Default `Worktrees.BasePath` migrated from `~/.workspaces/<project>` to
  `~/.thrum/worktrees/<project>`. Repos with an explicit `worktrees.base_path`
  in `.thrum/config.json` are unaffected. Pin the legacy path with
  `thrum config set worktrees.base_path "$HOME/.workspaces/<project>"` to
  preserve existing worktrees.
- tmux gate — if `tmux` is not on `PATH` when the wizard reaches the
  daemon-start step, init exits early with an OS-appropriate install hint.
- The inbox-check hook script is now correctly excluded alongside
  the startup script in `.gitignore` (and `.git/info/exclude` in stealth
  mode).

New in v0.9.2:
- Role configuration system — `/thrum:configure-roles` answers
  persist under a new `role_config` top-level key in `.thrum/config.json`
  (per-role autonomy + scope + rendered_hash; top-level schema_version).
  `thrum roles refresh` regenerates `.thrum/role_templates/<role>.md` from
  saved answers + the shipped templates embedded in the binary.
  `thrum prime` surfaces three drift hints: `roles.config.migration`
  (rendered templates exist but no role_config), `roles.config.schema-bump`
  (shipped schema_version > saved), and `roles.config.body-diff` (shipped
  body_hash != saved rendered_hash). Precedence: migration > schema-bump >
  body-diff.
- SessionStart identity banner + auto-load directive — Claude Code sessions
  launched via `thrum tmux create` and restarted via `thrum tmux restart`
  show a pane-side identity banner and a size-aware `MUST-READ` directive
  pointing at the briefing. The plugin SessionStart hook also injects
  `thrum prime` output via `additionalContext` so the briefing reaches the
  model even when the pane is small. Restart-snapshot framing is hoisted to
  the top of `additionalContext` and rephrased as a directive.
- tmux session scoping — `thrum tmux status` and `thrum tmux
  connect` now scope to the current daemon via a `@thrum-thrum-dir` tag,
  no longer leaking sessions across worktrees and projects. Migration:
  pre-0.9.2 sessions need to be recreated via `thrum tmux create` to appear
  in pass-2 output.
- tmux pty leak fix — tmux-exec migrated from `respawn-pane`
  to a persistent-session pool with flock-based coordination (portable
  fallback when flock is unavailable), eliminating fd-leak crashes on
  long-running daemons.
- Preamble fallback fixes — `runPreambleInit`
  fallback now follows `.thrum/redirect`; rendered preamble paths to
  strategy files are absolute, not relative.

## Quick Start

  thrum init                                          # Set up .thrum/ in repo
  thrum daemon start                                  # Start background daemon
  thrum worktree create <agent-name>                  # Agent work happens in a worktree; the main repo refuses new-agent binds
  cd <worktree-path>                                  # path printed by worktree create ("Worktree created at <path>")
  thrum quickstart --name <agent-name> --role planner --module auth        # Register + start session (run inside the worktree)
  echo 'Starting work on auth module' | thrum send --to <agent-name> -  # Send a message (positional body is refused)
  thrum inbox                                          # Check messages
  thrum sent                                           # Check sent items and receipts

## Global Flags

All commands accept these flags:

  --role VALUE        Agent role (or THRUM_ROLE env var)
  --module VALUE      Agent module (or THRUM_MODULE env var)
  --json              JSON output for scripting
  --quiet             Suppress non-essential output
  --verbose           Debug output

## All Commands

### Setup & Orientation

  thrum init [--force] [--stealth] [--runtime claude|codex|cursor|antigravity|copilot|muse|opencode|cli-only|all] [--dry-run] [--skills] [--agent-name NAME] [--agent-role ROLE] [--agent-module MODULE]
    Initialize Thrum in the current repository. Optionally generate runtime-specific configs.
    --skills installs just the thrum skill without full runtime configuration.
    Populates the `identity` block in config.json (daemon_id generated once via Bootstrap; idempotent).
    G2 guard: refuses non-git CWD; --force bypasses.

  thrum worktree setup WORKTREE_NAME
    Configure a feature worktree with .thrum/redirect to share the main issue database. Alias for `thrum worktree create`.

  thrum setup claude-md [--apply] [--force]
    Install or manage a Thrum-managed block in ./CLAUDE.md. Default: prints template to stdout.
    --apply: writes to ./CLAUDE.md. Creates file with template-only content if missing.
             Appends blank-line + template at end if file exists without a Thrum block.
             Errors if a Thrum block already present (exit 1, stderr message asks for --force).
    --force (with --apply): replaces the existing Thrum block in place. Idempotent.
    Block markers: <!-- BEGIN THRUM --> ... <!-- END THRUM --> (single space, no version, no trailing dot).
    Template is intentionally minimal (~30-40 lines): what Thrum is, 5 essential commands
    (whoami/team/inbox/send/reply), quickstart pointer.
    Use this ONLY when NOT running the Claude Code Thrum plugin — the plugin already
    injects messaging instructions via SessionStart hook + skills + slash commands.
    The CLAUDE.md path is for Claude Code without the plugin, or other runtimes (codex,
    cursor, opencode). Use one or the other, not both.

  thrum quickstart --name <agent-name> --role ROLE --module MODULE [--display NAME] [--intent TEXT] [--runtime PRESET] [--dry-run] [--force] [--no-init] [--preamble-file PATH]
    Register agent, start session, generate runtime config, and set intent in one step.
    Runtime presets: claude, codex, opencode, cursor, copilot, antigravity, muse, shell.
    --runtime writes `preferred_runtime` to the identity file (used by `thrum tmux launch`).
    G1a guard: refuses self-rename (caller already owns an identity in this worktree); --force bypasses.
    G1b guard: refuses name collision with a live foreign PID; --force bypasses.

  thrum overview [--json]
    Show combined status: identity, work context, team, inbox, sync.

  thrum whoami [--json]
    Show current agent identity (lightweight, no daemon required).

  thrum version
    Show version, build hash, repository URL, and documentation URL.

  thrum prime [--json]
    Gather comprehensive session context for agent initialization or context recovery.
    Shows: identity, session, team, inbox summary, branch, daemon status, commands, listener instruction.
    G5 guard: must be called from the topmost runtime process, not from inside another agent's process tree.

  thrum completion [bash|fish|powershell|zsh]
    Generate shell autocompletion scripts.

### Messaging

  thrum send [--scope type:value] [--ref type:value] [--mention @agent_name] [--thread ID] --to @agent_name [--to @agent_name ...] [--format markdown|plain|json] [--structured JSON] --stdin | --body-file FILE
    Send a message. --to accepts an explicit @agent_name only and is repeatable
    for multiple recipients. --broadcast and
    @everyone were removed by design — there is no
    one-to-many fan-out, name every recipient explicitly or address a scoped
    agent-type group. A positional MESSAGE argument is REFUSED
    (messaging.refuse_positional_body) — pass the body via --stdin (quoted
    heredoc: --stdin <<'EOF' ... EOF, or pipe: echo '...' | thrum send --to @x -)
    or --body-file FILE.

  thrum reply MSG_ID [--format markdown|plain|json] --stdin | --body-file FILE
    Reply to a message, copying the parent's audience (mentions/scopes). Includes
    reply_to reference. Same positional-body refusal as `send` — use --stdin or --body-file.

  thrum inbox [--scope type:value] [--mentions] [--unread] [--all|-a] [--page-size N] [--limit N] [--page N]
    List messages in your inbox. Auto-filters to messages addressed to you.
    Use --all to disable auto-filtering and show everything.

  thrum sent [--to @agent] [--unread] [--page-size N] [--limit N] [--page N]
    List messages you sent, including resolved recipients and durable read state.
    Use 'thrum message get <message-id>' for full details on one message.

  thrum wait [--timeout DURATION] [--scope type:value] [--mention ROLE] [--after OFFSET]
    Block until a matching message arrives. --mention filters incoming messages by
    a stored mention tag (read-side filter only — not a send-side fan-out mechanism).
    --after sign convention: negative (e.g., -30s) = include messages sent up to N ago; positive (e.g., +60s) = only messages N in the future; omit for "now". Exit 0=received, 1=timeout, 2=error.

### Message Management

  thrum message get MSG_ID
    Get a single message with full details.

  thrum message edit MSG_ID --stdin | --body-file FILE
    Edit a message (full replacement, author only). Positional body REFUSED — use --stdin or --body-file.

  thrum message delete MSG_ID --force
    Delete a message.

  thrum message read [MSG_ID...] [--all [--apply|--force]]
    Mark messages as read. `--all` alone is a dry run (lists candidates, marks nothing);
    `--all --apply` marks the already-seen candidates; `--all --force` marks ALL unread
    (needs a fresh `--all` dry run first).

  thrum purge --before DURATION|DATE [--confirm]
  thrum purge --all [--confirm]
    Remove old messages, sessions, and events. Without --confirm, shows a preview.
    Supports relative durations (2d, 24h), dates (2026-03-15), and RFC 3339.
    Cleans both SQLite and sync JSONL files. Agents are not touched.
    WARNING: fleet-wide history erasure, not a local disk trim — also trims the
    git-synced JSONL lanes (messages-v2/, sessions-v2/, receipts/) and emits a
    purge.executed event so every peer auto-purges to the same cutoff. The local
    events.jsonl journal is NOT trimmed (local-only, never synced). Always
    preview (no --confirm) first.

### Agent Identity

  thrum agent register --role ROLE --module MODULE [--name NAME] [--display NAME] [--force] [--re-register]
    Register this agent. Identity priority: THRUM_NAME env > --name flag > identity file.

  thrum agent whoami
    Show current agent identity and active session.

  thrum team [@AGENT] [--role ROLE] [--module MODULE] [--phase PHASE] [--include-inactive] [--offline] [--all] [--compact]
    Show the agent roster and work context for the selected scope.

  thrum agent delete NAME
    Delete an agent (removes identity, messages, SQLite record).

  thrum agent cleanup <agent-id>... [--force] [--dry-run]
    Check the named agents for orphan status and remove the orphaned ones. IDs are required;
    cleanup never selects deletion targets itself.

  thrum agent set-status <working|idle|blocked> [--agent NAME]       # v0.8.0
    Set agent operational status. Without --agent, updates local identity directly.
    With --agent, sends RPC to daemon to update a remote agent's identity file.
    Daemon uses this for auto-nudge detection: if pane is silent but status is
    "working", daemon nudges on next silence event.

### Agent Lifecycle (sleep / wake / retire / restore / resurrect)

  thrum agent sleep --agent NAME [--reason TEXT] [--force]
    (alias: park) Sleep ceremony: staleness check, self-healing PARK GATE
    directive, /thrum:restart snapshot directive, tmux teardown + queue drain,
    then emits agent.phase.transition {to: "sleeping"}. Does NOT pack a vault
    blob — that's a retirement artifact, not a sleep artifact.

  thrum agent wake --agent NAME
    Wake ceremony: collision check, tmux create in the agent's recorded
    worktree, tmux launch, wait for pane ready, inject the capstone trigger
    context, then emits agent.phase.transition {from: "sleeping", to: "active"}.
    Requires the agent to have a vault blob (written by sleep); otherwise
    escalates to the coordinator.

  thrum agent retire --agent NAME [--reason TEXT]
    Retire ceremony for a sleeping agent: operator-only gate, precondition
    that the agent is already sleeping, then emits agent.phase.transition
    {from: "sleeping", to: "retired"}. No vault blob (agent vault storage was
    removed); --successor is refused.

  thrum agent restore --agent NAME [--reason TEXT]
    Restore a retired agent back to 'sleeping' (never reactivates directly —
    run `thrum agent wake --agent NAME` separately afterward). Warm path: State.md present
    on disk, just flips phase. Cold path: State.md absent, pulls the blob from
    the vault first.

  thrum agent resurrect --agent NAME
    Resurrect a stale agent whose process crashed with no snapshot: rebuilds
    the restart snapshot from the agent's runtime transcript JSONL (no vault
    blob involved, unlike restore), recreates the worktree if absent, re-
    attaches the recorded branch if it still exists. Refuses while the
    agent's process is still alive. Does not change phase directly — run
    `thrum agent wake --agent NAME` afterward to make the agent active.

  thrum agent state update | recover | last-session
    Manage scheduled-agent state.md: update records a completed session
    (skill-driven), recover repairs a corrupt state.md (skill-driven), and
    last-session prints the newest recorded session field (read-only).

  thrum agent sessions list [agent-id] | archive <agent-id>
    Manage archived session snapshots. list shows archived sessions for an
    agent; archive invokes the session.archive RPC directly (debug only).

  thrum agent runtime-config get <agent-name> | set <agent-name> [--model MODEL] [--effort EFFORT]
    Manage per-agent runtime configuration (model, effort). get prints the
    current pin; set writes (or clears, with an empty value) the fields.

### Sessions

  thrum session start
    Start a new work session (agent must be registered).

  thrum session end [--reason normal|crash] [--session-id ID]
    End current session.

  thrum session list [--active] [--agent AGENT_ID]
    List all sessions. --active shows only active sessions.

  thrum session heartbeat [--add-scope type:value] [--remove-scope type:value] [--add-ref type:value] [--remove-ref type:value]
    Send heartbeat. Triggers git context extraction, updates last-seen time.

  thrum session set-intent TEXT
    Set work intent for current session. Pass "" to clear.

  thrum session set-task TASK
    Set current task identifier. Pass "" to clear.

### Team Overview

  thrum team [@AGENT] [--all|--daemon ID|--hostname HOST|--tmux_session PREFIX] [--offline] [--phase PHASE] [--system] [--json]
    Show rich status for active agents (sessions, context, inbox, branches).
    Default (no scope flag): THIS DAEMON ONLY. ⚠️ BREAKING (was: whole fleet) —
    use --daemon ID to ask another daemon.
    @AGENT switches to the expanded single-agent view. It is fleet-wide and
    index-backed (instant PK lookup) — an agent under the same name on a
    different daemon is always found; it can no longer be silently missed.
    Exactly one scope selector may be active at a time: @AGENT, --daemon,
    --hostname, --tmux_session, --all are mutually exclusive (passing two errors).
    --all         Every agent in this daemon's database, unfiltered, without contacting
                  other daemons (--daemon ID asks one daemon). ⚠️ BREAKING: used to
                  mean "include offline" only (local scope); now shows every agent here,
                  including offline. To include offline agents within the LOCAL
                  scope only, use --offline instead.
    --offline     Include offline agents within whichever scope is active
                  (modifier, composes with any scope selector — not itself a
                  scope selector).
    --daemon ID       One daemon by id, fleet-wide. Unknown id errors, naming
                      the known daemon ids (no more silent empty list).
    --hostname HOST   All agents on one host, fleet-wide. Unknown hostname
                      errors the same way.
    --tmux_session PREFIX   All agents whose tmux session name starts with
                            PREFIX, fleet-wide. Prefix multi-match — e.g.
                            'thrum' can return every coordinator sharing a
                            'thrum*' session. Ignores the trailing :pane suffix.
    --phase PHASE   Filter to one lifecycle phase: active|warm-hold|sleeping|
                    retired|stale|modal-blocked. Modifier — composes with
                    whichever scope is active. Typos error.
                    --phase retired is the only way to see tombstoned agents.
    --system      Include reserved pseudo-agents. ⊙ glyph marks them
                  (e.g. @supervisor_<project>).
    List and expanded views now show each agent's full worktree path
    (was: basename only) — enough to cd directly into it.

### Context Management

  thrum state set --kind KIND --scope SCOPE (--value JSON | --stdin | --value-file PATH)
    Upsert one of your personal state entries (agent-local current state).

  thrum state list [--kind KIND] [--agent ID]
    List state entries; defaults to your own agent-local entries.

  thrum queue list [--agent ID] [--status STATUS] [--stage STAGE]
    List your committed-work queue bundles, or another agent's with --agent.

### Coordination

  thrum who-has FILE
    Check which agents are editing a file.

  thrum ping AGENT
    Check if an agent is online (with or without @ prefix).

### Sync

  thrum sync status
    Show sync loop status and last sync time.

  thrum sync force
    Trigger immediate sync (non-blocking).

  thrum sync enable | disable
    Master sync on/off switch; takes effect on next daemon restart.

  thrum sync mechanism <a-sync|peer|email> <full|directed>
    Set a sync mechanism's scope; takes effect on next daemon restart.

  thrum sync mechanism remove <a-sync|peer|email>
    Delete a mechanism (all scopes), keep enabled. Local-only stanza (not
    fleet-replicated, unlike sync_via_git); takes effect on next daemon
    restart. Fails while sync_via_git is explicitly true (git sync would stay
    on): set it false, or pass --force to remove anyway.

  thrum sync quickstart [name]
    Register, start session, and set intent in one step.

  thrum sync backfill-shards
    Immediately backfill memory-record-v2 shards from all registered peers
    (Phase-2-direct).

### Peer Management (Cross-Repo, v0.7.0)

  thrum peer add --type TYPE [--label LABEL]
    Start a pairing session. Displays a 16-digit peercode. Blocks until peer connects (5min timeout).
    --label is required in non-interactive mode (interactive TTY prompts otherwise). THRUM_TS_AUTHKEY must be in the daemon's env (via .thrum/.env or repo .env); 'thrum daemon restart' does not re-source .env.
    --type is MANDATORY (BREAKING in v0.9.0). Values: tailscale, local, network, repair.
    Peer listeners are OFF by default: the Tailscale listener runs only if tailscale.listen is true (config key; env THRUM_TS_LISTENER overrides) or, when unset, the box already has paired tailscale peers; --type network needs lan.listen / THRUM_LAN_LISTENER likewise (or existing network peers/endpoints). An explicit false wins over existing peers. A peer add/join of an off transport is refused with the exact key, env var and 'restart the daemon' instructions; restart the daemon after changing either switch.
    Host mode (default): with the Tailscale app installed thrum binds a single 100.64.0.0/10 host IP (no var/tsnet). Persist the mode with thrum config set tailscale.mode host|embedded (machine-local; env THRUM_TS_MODE overrides; an invalid value fails daemon boot loudly; embedded means no host-IP listener). On multi-tailnet hosts pin the reachable IP persistently via thrum config set tailscale.primary_ip <ip> (or env THRUM_PEER_LISTEN_IP alias THRUM_TS_LISTEN_IP for emergency); verify with 'thrum daemon status' + 'tailscale status'. Fail-closed: with multiple CGNAT IPs and no pin (no env and no tailscale.primary_ip), the daemon advertises no peer listener (ambiguous — status shows candidates and required pin). Machine-enforced: 'peer join' automatically TCP-dials the peercode IP:port before consuming the window and fails with an actionable unreachable-endpoint error if not reachable. Preflight from the JOINER: nc -z <advertised-ip> <port> before consuming the 5-min window. Never use 'tailscale down/logout' as workaround.

  thrum peer join [peercode] [--peercode CODE] [--repo-path PATH] --type TYPE
    Connect to a remote peer using the peercode from `peer add` (peercode carries the destination; no --addr flag for tailscale). The joiner dials the adder's advertised IP:port — it must be reachable from the joiner's tailnet.
    Peercode format: name:ip:port:code. Accepts positional arg, --peercode flag, stdin pipe, or interactive prompt.
    Use --repo-path for local same-machine peers (sets transport to "local").
    --type is MANDATORY (BREAKING in v0.9.0). Values: tailscale, local, network, repair.
    repair type is peer join only; used for drift reconciliation without a new peercode.
    Multi-tailnet: the adder pins THRUM_PEER_LISTEN_IP (fail-closed without pin); the joiner proves reachability automatically via TCP dial before consuming the window (also manually with nc -z <ip> <port>). Only the joiner can prove it — adder's LocalAPI may see a different tailnet. Successful inbound pairing/dial or peer-health observation may then mark reachable; local bind/env never does.

  thrum peer list [--json]
    List paired peers with address, last sync, sequence number.
    drift_reconcile_failed peers show an inline └─ hint row with remediation command.

  thrum peer remove <name>
    Remove a paired peer. Stops syncing immediately.

  thrum peer status [--json]
    Show detailed per-peer health: pairing time, auth status, sync state.

  thrum peer configure [<peer-name>] <action> <agent-name> [--daemon-id ID]
    Manage proxy agents for a peer. Actions: add-agent, remove-agent.
    A name shared by several peers is refused and lists their daemon IDs;
    --daemon-id picks one (<peer-name> may then be omitted).
    Proxy agents appear locally as prefix:name (e.g., sf:coordinator_1).
    TROUBLESHOOTING unknown-recipient bounces: if `thrum send --to @<agent>`
    on a paired box bounces with unknown recipient (the agent lives on the
    PEER, not locally — it is absent from the local agents table), register
    it as a proxy agent on the SENDING side first:
      thrum peer configure <peer-name> add-agent <agent-name>
    Then send to @<agent-name> (or @<peer-prefix>:<agent-name>). Cross-peer
    addressing is not auto-discovered; each side must add-agent the remote
    agents it wants to address.

    Reaching an agent on a daemon you are not paired with: a message routes
    through a directly paired peer, never by pairing with the target daemon.
    The sending daemon resolves a recipient from its local agents and from the
    agents registered on its directly paired peers only. For an agent that
    lives on a daemon you are not paired with, run once on the SENDING daemon,
    per remote agent, naming the directly paired peer that knows the agent:
      thrum peer configure <relay-peer-name> add-agent <agent-name>
    Then thrum send --to @<agent-name> routes through that peer. Do this on
    each side that needs to send. Check pairing with thrum peer list (direct
    peers only) and delivery with thrum message get <id>, which shows
    (delivered) per recipient.
    Not the fix: pairing the two daemons with each other. Not needed for
    delivery: thrum peer relayed add and thrum peer relayed grant, which
    govern what a daemon accepts from a relayed origin. Notes: relayed add
    --via takes daemon IDs, not peer names; relayed grant does not validate
    the capability key (the messaging key is can_send_messages).
    After add-agent, the supervisor may report "Unresolved agent records" for
    the proxy rows: reconcile asks the relay, which refuses with "owned by
    daemon X ... no second hop". A build with the reconcile owner pointer
    follows the named owner once and the warning clears; older builds keep
    the warning. Do NOT delete those rows as the supervisor suggests: deleting
    them removes the routing.

  thrum peer grant[<peer-name>] [--daemon-id ID] [--capabilities KEYS] [--revoke KEYS]
    Grant (--capabilities) or revoke (--revoke) capability keys for a peer.
    KEYS is comma-separated snake_case keys, e.g. can_mirror_tmux; --capabilities
    all grants every owner-exposed capability. Keys not named keep their value.
    A change reaches an open connection at its next gate check; no reconnect.
    A request relayed through another peer needs two grants on this daemon: on
    the relay can_relay_<cap> (when that key is unset the relay's plain can_<cap>
    applies; an explicit false denies) AND can_<cap> on the origin (paired with this
    daemon directly, or recorded with thrum peer relayed add). Granting to a peer with no positive
    direct-connection signal still applies and prints a warning on stderr.
    When two peers share a name the name is refused and lists their daemon IDs;
    --daemon-id picks one (the name is then optional; the daemon ID wins).

  thrum peer relayed add <origin> --via <relay>[,<hop>...]
    Record an origin reachable only through a directly paired relay. --via is the
    relay first, then the hops toward the origin; the route is echoed as
    route: <relay> -> <hop> -> <origin>. A relayed origin has no grants until you
    grant them, and a grant admits it only on that exact route.

  thrum peer relayed list
    List active relayed origins with their routes and explicit grants (read-only).

  thrum peer relayed grant <origin> <capability> [--off]
    Grant (or with --off, deny) one can_ capability on a relayed origin.

  thrum peer relayed remove <origin>
    Revoke the active relayed record for an origin. The record stays in peers.json,
    ended, and is no longer matched. A removed relay revokes every record whose route
    names it.

  thrum peer deny [<peer-name>] [--daemon-id ID] [--can-share-ui] [--can-share-storage] [--can-write-substrate-folder]
    Explicitly deny a default-allow capability for a peer. Undo with
    thrum peer grant <peer-name> --capabilities <key>. --daemon-id picks the
    peer when its name is shared by several peers.

  thrum peer set-coordinator [<peer>] <agent-name> [--daemon-id ID]
    Set (or clear, with an empty agent-name) the coordinator agent ID for a peer.
    A name shared by several peers is refused and lists their daemon IDs;
    --daemon-id picks one (<peer> may then be omitted).

  thrum peer repin
    Rotate the mTLS root CA and push the new root to reachable peers.

  thrum peer upgrade-mtls [<peer-name>] [--daemon-id ID]
    Trigger an in-band mTLS upgrade for an already-paired 0.11 peer.
    A name shared by several peers is refused and lists their daemon IDs;
    --daemon-id picks one (<peer-name> may then be omitted).

  thrum peer migrate-proxies
    Excise phantom/nested proxy records from the agents table.

  thrum peer monitor
    One-shot peer health sweep; routes ALARMs to the coordinator.

  thrum peer victim-monitor
    Victim-side peer staleness sweep (0.10.6-compatible).

  thrum peer audit
    Show the peer lifecycle audit log (peer_* ops from audit.jsonl).

  thrum peer backup-trust [--out DIR]
    Back up connection-trust files (peers.json, CA keys, tsnet state).

  thrum peer restore-trust <backup-dir>
    Restore connection-trust files from a backup directory produced by
    `thrum peer backup-trust`. Verifies SHA-256 checksums before writing.

### Single-Agent Mode (v0.7.0)

  thrum single-agent-mode [true|false|on|off]
    Toggle or query single-agent mode. Without args, prints current mode.
    When enabled: no listener, no cron watchdog, no stop hook, no messaging protocol.
    Context features (prime, sessions, restart snapshots) still work.
    Default for new repos after thrum init.

### Runtime Presets

  thrum runtime list
    List all runtime presets (claude, codex, opencode, cursor, copilot, antigravity, muse, shell).

  thrum runtime show <name>
    Show details for a runtime preset.

  thrum runtime set-default <name>
    Set the default runtime preset.

  thrum runtime detect [--json]
    List the agent runtimes detected for the repository (repo marker, environment variable or verified binary).
    --json prints an array of {"name","tier","source"} objects ([] when none). thrum tunnel runs it on the remote.

  OpenCode plugin compatibility:
    Tested with OpenCode 1.18.x; OpenCode 2.x is not supported yet because it
    lacks the `-m` flag and has plugin API changes. Pro install:
    `opencode plugin opencode-thrum-pro --global -f`.

### Role Templates

  thrum roles list
    List role templates and matching agents.

  thrum roles deploy [--agent NAME] [--dry-run]
    Re-render preambles for registered agents from role templates. Full overwrite.

  thrum roles refresh
    Regenerate .thrum/role_templates/<role>.md from saved answers.

  thrum roles templates print <role>-<autonomy>
    Print an embedded shipped role template (with frontmatter), e.g.
    `thrum roles templates print implementer-strict`.

  thrum roles save-config
    Write role_config to .thrum/config.json from JSON on stdin.

  thrum roles configure
    Configure role templates from flags or detected agent roles (no AI required).
    Re-renders .thrum/role_templates/<role>.md and re-appends the repo-root
    role-rules/<role>.md, so those rules survive while hand edits to the
    generated template are replaced. --deploy then pushes to registered agents.

### Configuration

  thrum config show [--json]
    Show effective configuration from all sources (config.json, env, defaults).

  thrum config set tailscale.listen <true|false|on|off|"">   (machine-local; local unix socket only)
  thrum config set lan.listen <true|false|on|off|"">         (machine-local; local unix socket only)
    Turn the Tailscale / LAN peer listener on or off. Both are OFF by default unless peers of that transport already
    exist (implicit on, so upgraded fleet boxes keep working); an explicit false wins over existing peers; "" clears
    the key to unset. Env THRUM_TS_LISTENER / THRUM_LAN_LISTENER override the config key. Restart the daemon for either
    to take effect. 'thrum daemon status' shows "Tailscale listener: ..." and "LAN listener: ..." lines.

  thrum config hook-guard [status|on|off] [--json]
    Show or switch the opt-in PreToolUse hook guard (off by default; per box).
    'off' needs a coordinator or a human. Emergency disable without the daemon:
    THRUM_HOOKLOG_GUARD=off, or "hook_guard": {"enabled": false} in .thrum/config.json.

### Account usage (quota-axi)

  Off by default. daemon.account_usage_quota_axi=true in .thrum/config.json makes the daemon run the pinned
  quota-axi (0.1.68, found on the daemon's own PATH, never installed by the daemon) every 15 minutes and show used /
  remaining / reset time per account in 'thrum team' (Accounts section). daemon.account_usage_runtimes picks which
  runtimes are read (default claude, codex, cursor, copilot; muse, antigravity and opencode only when listed).
  Both keys are read at daemon start ('thrum daemon restart'). A daemon without a reading shows "Usage not enabled on
  daemon". Setup steps, per-runtime credentials and failure states: the setting-up-account-usage skill.

### Permission Supervisors

  What it does: the daemon watches the tmux pane of every agent it runs for
  permission prompts (a runtime waiting on an approval modal) and sends a
  nudge message to the configured supervisors so the agent is not left stuck.

  How agents get monitored: monitoring covers agents launched with the
  standard thrum commands (`thrum tmux create` / `thrum tmux launch`). Each
  one is enrolled in the prompt scanner automatically at launch; there is no
  per-agent opt-in and nothing extra to configure. Launch agents with these
  commands — do not start agent panes by other means and try to get them
  detected.

  Who is notified: the agents/users listed in permission_supervisors (step 1
  below). The nudge is sent by the @supervisor_<project> pseudo-agent.

  How often: each monitored pane is checked every 10 seconds. When a prompt
  is found, the first nudge goes out immediately; if the prompt is still
  there, reminders follow at +5 min, +15 min, +45 min, +2 h and +4 h after
  first detection (6 nudges total). After the last one the agent is marked
  stuck and no further nudges are sent. These timings are fixed, not
  configurable.

  One-time setup for a new repo (run by the repo's coordinator):

  1. thrum config set permission_supervisors '["coordinator"]'
       Who receives permission-prompt nudges. Entries may be role names
       (fans out to every active agent with that role), @agent names
       (e.g. "@coordinator_1"), or @user: names (e.g. "@user:jane-doe";
       forwarded to Telegram if the bridge is configured). A human-only
       list such as ["@user:jane-doe"] is valid; a coordinator entry is
       not required. thrum init writes ["@user:<name>"] (the init user's
       git user.name in slug form) by default, and writes nothing when
       user.name is unset. Default when the key is unset: ["coordinator"].

  2. thrum config set project_name my-project        (optional)
       Names the @supervisor_<project> pseudo-agent that sends the nudges.
       The pseudo-agent is registered at daemon boot, so run
       thrum daemon restart after changing project_name.

  3. No daemon restart is needed for permission_supervisors: the config is
     re-read on every nudge.

  4. Verify:
       grep permission_supervisors .thrum/config.json  -> shows your list
       thrum team --system         -> @supervisor_<project> listed (⊙ glyph)

  After this, agents launched via `thrum tmux create` / `thrum tmux launch`
  are monitored automatically; no further configuration or restart is
  needed for them.

### Tmux Session Management (v0.7.1)

  thrum tmux create <name> --cwd <path> --name <agent-name> --role ROLE --module MODULE [--intent TEXT] [--runtime PRESET] [--model MODEL] [--effort EFFORT] [--mode MODE] [--identity TYPE] [--force] [--no-agent]
    Create a tmux session for an agent with clean environment and monitor-silence hooks.
    --name, --role, --module are required (or pass --no-agent to skip registration).
    Runs `thrum quickstart` inside the pane automatically after creating the session.
    --intent, --runtime, --model, --effort, --mode, --identity, --force are passed through to quickstart.
    --model / --effort here only WRITE the pin into runtime_config — they do NOT
    apply it. The runtime is not started by `create`. Pass the SAME --model /
    --effort to `thrum tmux launch` too — launch is what actually resolves and
    renders them, and create's write is async, so `create`-only is a race that
    can silently lose the pin.

  thrum tmux quickstart <name> --cwd <path> --name <agent-name> --role ROLE --module MODULE [...]
    Alias for `thrum tmux create`.

  thrum tmux launch <name> [--runtime PRESET] [--model MODEL] [--effort EFFORT]
    Start an AI tool inside an existing tmux session. Default runtime: claude.
    PRESET: claude, opencode, codex, cursor, shell, etc.
    --model: pin the runtime LLM model (e.g. haiku|sonnet|opus); overrides runtime_config model.
    --effort: pin reasoning effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max); overrides runtime_config effort.
    This is where the model/effort pin actually resolves and gets rendered into
    the launched command — always pass --model/--effort here, not only to `create`.

  thrum tmux status
    Show all tmux-managed sessions with agent info, state, runtime, and branch.

  thrum tmux list
    Alias for thrum tmux status.

  thrum tmux kill <name>
    Tear down a tmux session and clear tmux_session from identity file.

  thrum tmux send <name> [<text>] [--keys K1,K2,...]
    Two modes. With <text>: send literal text plus a trailing Enter. With
    --keys: deliver named tmux keys (Enter, Escape, Up, Down, Left, Right,
    Tab, digits, ...) in order — the primitive for driving a modal/permission
    prompt to a specific selection (e.g. picking "Allow always") without a
    human attach. Keys are comma-separated or the flag repeated; bounded to 32
    keys per call. Both modes route through the peer-routed tmux.send RPC, so
    --keys works identically against a LOCAL or a REMOTE/peer session
    (fleet-wide). This supersedes the retired local-only tmux-key primitive.
    Examples:
      thrum tmux send mysession "hello"
      thrum tmux send mysession --keys Right,Tab,Enter
      thrum tmux send mysession --keys Escape

  thrum tmux capture <name> [--lines N] [--format raw|annotated|json]
    Capture pane content from a tmux session. --ctx and --state return
    JSON observations instead; --daemon-id disambiguates a peer name.

  thrum tmux restart <name> [--force] [--runtime R] [--resume]
    Restart a tmux session. Graceful restart asks the agent to save a snapshot
    and waits up to restart.graceful_timeout; timeout records no snapshot.
    Force skips the save request and creates no snapshot; an existing snapshot
    may still be used. Resume skips the Thrum snapshot phase and asks the same
    pinned runtime to resume its vendor session. Resume refuses --force,
    --runtime, and --model (RPC also refuses provider). Some ID discovery sends
    /exit and may close the current runtime process; Thrum resolves the worktree
    before discovery.
    Either non-resume flow replaces the tmux session; a snapshot is loaded by prime if present.

  thrum tmux connect [name]
    Attach to a running agent's tmux session. With a name, attaches directly;
    without one, lists alive sessions and lets you pick.

  thrum tmux model-select <session> <model-name> [--effort EFFORT] [--dry-run]
    Drive the runtime's /model selector in a session to the named model. The
    daemon auto-resolves the runtime from the session's identity file.
    --dry-run: print the key-press plan without sending it.

  thrum tmux wait-pane-ready <session> [--ceiling SECONDS] [--runtime RUNTIME]
    Block until the session's pane (window 0, pane 0) reaches interactive/ready
    state (silence-driven detection, not a blind timer) and is not at a
    trust-gate or permission dialog. Exit 0 when ready and safe; exit 1 when
    the ceiling elapses or the pane is unsafe. Use after `thrum tmux launch`
    to gate further keystrokes on confirmed readiness.
    --ceiling: maximum wait in seconds (default 90).

  thrum tmux check-pane <session> [--repo PATH]
    Hidden; called by tmux hooks. Checks a pane for permission prompts or idle
    state. --repo is deprecated/unused — the daemon resolves identity.

  thrum tmux supervise <session> [--cwd PATH] [--runtime RUNTIME] [--parent AGENT]
    Internal — invoked by `thrum monitor`, not run directly. Grace-windowed
    liveness supervision for a persistent watcher's tmux session; can cold-start
    the session from --cwd/--runtime if absent, and notifies --parent via
    `thrum send` when the supervised session's agent_status reads stuck.

### Tmux Command Queue (v0.8.0)

  thrum tmux queue <session> <command> [--timeout SECONDS] [--wait] [--silence FLOAT]
    Submit a command to a tmux session's queue. Daemon dispatches FIFO when the
    pane goes silent, detects completion via next silence event, captures output.
    - --timeout: command timeout in seconds (default: 120)
    - --wait: block until the command reaches a terminal state; suppresses @system notification
    - --silence: silence threshold in seconds (server default: 5.0)
    Without --wait: returns command_id immediately; sends @system inbox message on completion,
    timeout, cancellation, or interruption.

  thrum tmux queue-status <session> [--json]
    Show the active command and queued commands for a session.

  thrum tmux cancel <command-id>
    Cancel a queued or active command.

### Worktree Management (v0.8.0)

  thrum worktree create <name> [-b BRANCH] [--base REF | --from REF] [--detach] [--name <agent-name> --role ROLE --module MODULE] [--intent TEXT] [--runtime PRESET]
    Create a git worktree with Thrum and Beads redirect wiring. Worktree path:
    `worktrees.base_path/<name>` (default: ~/.thrum/worktrees/<project>/<name>).
    - -b / --branch: branch name (default: feature/<name>)
    - --base / --from REF: ref to start from (default: main repo HEAD or merge_target); errors if it does not resolve, if --base and --from differ, or if -b names an existing branch at a different commit (the base would be ignored)
    - --detach: create detached HEAD worktree at --base/--from; cannot be combined with -b
    - --name, --role, --module (all optional): if all three provided, creates a
      real tmux session with the worktree as cwd and runs quickstart inside the
      pane via SendKeys (PID-isolated, with daemon-side retry at 5s and CLI-side
      pane capture at 12s). The session is kept — start the runtime later with
      `thrum tmux launch <name>`. The CLI prints the next-step launch command.
    Sets up .thrum/redirect and .thrum/identities/ (if worktrees.thrum_enabled).
    Sets up .beads/redirect (if the main checkout has .beads/).
    v0.8.2: errors out if the resolved worktree path or worktrees.base_path is
    the repo root itself (repo-root guard).

  thrum worktree setup <name> [-b BRANCH] [--detach] [...]
    Alias for `thrum worktree create`.

  thrum worktree teardown <name|path>
    Retire the agent, kill its tmux session (a PATH kills only the sessions of
    agents whose identities live in that worktree), salvage .thrum state and remove the
    worktree (the agent row stays retired until `thrum agent delete`).
    NAME matches a registered worktree only when its parent directory is the
    worktree root or the legacy ~/.thrum/worktrees/<project> root (two matches
    refuse and list paths).
    PATH (contains /) names any registered git worktree of this repo, resolved
    from `git worktree list`. The identity guard refuses the main repo or another
    live agent's home unless --force-unsafe.
    Removes the worktree with a non-forced `git worktree remove <path>`.

  thrum worktree list
    List git worktrees with Thrum agent info (reads identity files to show
    which agent is active per worktree).

  thrum worktree adopt [path]
    Reconstruct .thrum/redirect for an unwired git worktree (e.g. one created
    by bare `git worktree add` instead of `thrum worktree create`, or `thrum
    init`). Non-destructive and idempotent — running it on an already-wired
    worktree succeeds silently.

### Move an agent to a different worktree (same machine)

  thrum agent rehome --name <agent-name> --to-daemon <own-daemon-id> --to-worktree <new-worktree-path> [--branch <branch>] [--reason "<text>"]
    Rebinds an agent's home worktree on this machine. Run it on this box, from
    the daemon that owns the agent. --branch and --reason are optional. --force
    skips the confirmation prompt.
    Get <own-daemon-id> from `thrum daemon status --json`, at `.identity.daemon_id`.
    The field is omitted when identity is unavailable.
    rehome changes the agent's registration only. It does not create the target
    worktree, copy local files, or relocate session transcripts. Create the new
    worktree first, with `thrum worktree create`.
    To retire the old worktree, run `thrum worktree teardown <name|path>`. Do not
    use raw `git worktree remove`.

### Monitor Jobs

  thrum monitor start --name <name> --match <regex> --to @<agent> [--cwd <dir>] [--debounce 60s] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--schedule <cron>] [--notify-on-success] -- <argv...>
    Spawn a long-running child process, or (with --schedule) run it one-shot per cron tick.
    Watch its stdout+stderr for lines matching the regex. Each match emits a synthetic
    Thrum message to the target agent. (`thrum monitor add` is an alias for `thrum monitor start`.)
    - --name: unique monitor name
    - --match: Go regex applied to each output line
    - --to: recipient agent (@name)
    - --cwd: working directory for the command (default: current directory)
    - --debounce: leading-edge debounce window (default: 60s, min: 30s)
    - --env KEY=VALUE: extra env vars for the child (repeatable; redacted in output)
    - --schedule: 5-field cron expression; runs one-shot per tick instead of continuously.
      `update --schedule` changes the cron of a scheduled monitor at any time; setting or
      removing a schedule switches the mode, which is refused while the monitor runs and
      allowed while it is stopped.
    - --notify-on-success: deliver a generic [OK] message for a successful run in which no
      line matched (a run that matched is reported by its matched lines)
    - -- <argv...>: command + args (no shell expansion; use explicit argv)
    Sender identity appears as `monitor:<name>` in the inbox.
    Monitors auto-persist and survive daemon restart.

  thrum monitor list [--all]
    List running monitors. --all includes stopped/dead <1wk.

  thrum monitor show <id|name>
    Show monitor config, status, and recent log lines.

  thrum monitor update <id|name> [--match <regex>] [--to @<agent>] [--debounce <duration>] [--schedule <cron>]
    Update match/schedule/target/debounce in place — no stop/start gap. Works on both
    running and stopped monitors; status is untouched. Only the flags you pass change;
    argv, cwd, and env are left byte-for-byte untouched. Cannot flip a monitor between
    continuous and scheduled mode.

  thrum monitor stop <id|name>
    Stop a monitor. Sends SIGTERM to the child process (SIGKILL after 5s). The monitor
    RECORD PERSISTS (visible in `monitor list --all` / `monitor show`) and reserves the
    name — `monitor start --name <same>` fails with "monitor name already in use" until
    you `monitor delete` it. `stop` on an already-stopped monitor fails.

  thrum monitor delete <id|name>
    Permanently remove a monitor, freeing its name for reuse. Accepts name or ID, running
    or stopped. This is the fix when a stopped monitor's name is blocking `start` — `stop`
    alone does not free it. Recreating the same name afterwards succeeds but gets a new ID.

  thrum monitor logs <id|name> [-n/--limit <n>]
    Historical lookup of a monitor's most recent matches (not a live tail). Default limit: 20.

  thrum monitor restart <id|name>
    Restart a stopped or failed monitor. Preserves the same ID. Works by name or ID.

### Monitor Jobs workflow

  # Watch a build log and ping the reviewer when tests fail
  thrum monitor start \
    --name build-watcher \
    --match "FAIL|panic:" \
    --to @reviewer \
    --debounce 120s \
    -- tail -F /var/log/ci/build.log

  # Check what's running
  thrum monitor list

  # Inspect recent matches
  thrum monitor logs build-watcher

  # Widen the match pattern without restarting
  thrum monitor update build-watcher --match "FAIL|panic:|ERROR"

  # Stop when done (record persists, name stays reserved)
  thrum monitor stop build-watcher

  # Free the name for reuse
  thrum monitor delete build-watcher

### Session Restart (v0.7.1)

  thrum tmux snapshot save [--reason self-initiated|external|context-threshold]
    Save conversation snapshot for session restart.

  thrum tmux snapshot restore
    Output restart snapshot to stdout and delete file. Manual escape hatch.

  thrum tmux snapshot check
    Check if a recoverable restart snapshot exists. Exit 0 = yes, exit 1 = no.

### Memory

  thrum memory create --kind KIND --title TEXT --oneline TEXT [--short TEXT|--full TEXT] [--tag a] [--scope SCOPE] [...]
    Create a new memory record (structured: decisions, lessons, references, notes).
    --kind/--title/--oneline required. --oneline max 280 bytes (single line);
    --short max 4 KB; --full max 256 KB. Each of --short/--full accepts a literal
    string, @path (read from file), or - (stdin). There is no --body flag.

  thrum memory show <id>
    Show a single memory record by ID.

  thrum memory list [--kind KIND] [--tags a,b] [--zoom oneline|...] [--limit N] [...]
    List memory records (paginated).

  thrum memory search [query...] [--near TEXT] [...]
    Search memory records (structured predicates + FTS5 grep; --near adds RAG ranking).

  thrum memory edit <id> [--flag fields...]
    Edit a memory record (patch-shaped — only passed --flag fields apply) (requires license).

  thrum memory delete <id> [--hard]
    Soft-delete a memory. --hard performs an irreversible purge and requires a confirm token.

  thrum memory link <from-id> <edge-kind> <to-id>
    Add an edge between two memory records (requires license).

  thrum memory unlink <from-id> <edge-kind> <to-id>
    Remove an edge between two memory records.

  thrum memory history <id>
    Show the JSONL audit trail for a memory record.

  thrum memory index
    List memory records as a one-line index (sugar for `list --zoom oneline`).

  thrum memory tags | kinds
    List observed tags / kinds with usage counts.

  thrum memory count
    Count memories in the three default-assembly buckets (you / role / other).

  thrum memory embed status | rebuild
    Inspect or rebuild the per-zoom embedding worker state. status shows queue
    depth + per-status/per-zoom counts; rebuild re-enqueues every active
    memory at all zoom levels for embedding.

  thrum memory graph | diag
    Graph-substrate diagnostics for the memory layer; diag shows the drift
    check between memory_record and graph node stores.

  Maintenance/one-shot subcommands (not for routine use): backfill-events,
  condense-section, migrate-from-bd, migrate-project-state [path],
  reproject, record-session, sync-section.

### Embed (local embedding models)

  Distinct from `thrum memory embed status | rebuild` above (worker state for
  the memory RAG pipeline) — this is model download/caching.

  thrum embed pull-model [--model bge-small-en-v1.5|jina-embeddings-v2-small-en] [--cache-dir PATH]
    Pre-download and cache a local embedding model for provider: local.
    Cached under <cacheDir>/thrum/embed-models/ (default: OS user cache dir).

### Issues (native task tracking)

  thrum issue add
    Create a new issue.

  thrum issue show
    Show details for a single issue.

  thrum issue list
    List issues.

  thrum issue ready
    List unblocked (ready) issues.

  thrum issue update
    Update an existing issue.

  thrum issue delete
    Delete (tombstone) an issue. Soft delete; no CLI restore in 0.11. Deleted issues still appear in issue show, issue list, and issue ready in 0.11 — the tombstone is not yet surfaced to those read paths.

  thrum issue close
    Close an issue.

  thrum issue dep BLOCKER_ID
    Add a dependency: BLOCKER_ID must close before BLOCKED_ID becomes ready.

  thrum issue dep-remove BLOCKER_ID
    Remove a dependency: BLOCKER_ID no longer blocks BLOCKED_ID.

  thrum issue comment
    Add a comment to an issue.

### State (agent-local and fleet current-value entries)

  A state entry is keyed by (kind, scope) — both free-form strings, addressed
  on the CLI as `<kind>:<scope>`. `kind` may be registered (declared threshold/
  tier via `state describe`) or ad-hoc. Two tiers: agent-local (private to the
  writing agent; `--agent` reads another agent's local entries) and fleet
  (shared current-value facts like a deploy SHA or topology row, peer-synced,
  append-only history via `state history`). `state set` always upserts by
  (kind, scope) — there is no merge; the new value fully replaces the old one
  at that key.

  GOTCHA — scope-string consistency: because scope is free-form, the SAME
  logical entity can be written under two different scope strings (e.g.
  `deploy_state:primary` vs `deploy_state:box:primary`) with no error and no
  warning. This does not overwrite the other row — it creates a SECOND,
  independent (kind, scope) entry. A freshness sweep or monitor reads one
  SPECIFIC key; if you re-assert under a different scope string than the one
  the reader uses, the reader keeps reading its own (now-stale) key and keeps
  firing false-stale alerts even though you believe you just re-asserted the
  row. Convention: use the plain entity name as the scope (`deploy_state:
  primary`, not `deploy_state:box:primary`) — the setter and the reader/
  monitor MUST use the identical scope key. If a freshness alert persists
  after you re-assert, run `thrum state list --kind <kind>` and look for
  duplicate/near-duplicate scopes naming the same entity.

  thrum state set --kind KIND --scope SCOPE (--value JSON | --stdin | --value-file PATH) [--as-of TIME] [--method by_effect|asserted|relayed] [--from-message] [--verify-cmd CMD] [--freshness-owner AGENT]
    Upsert a state entry (creates or overwrites). The value comes from exactly
    one of --value, --stdin, or --value-file; prefer --stdin or --value-file for
    prose. It must be well-formed JSON on every path. --as-of is the measurement
    time (fleet kinds only, RFC3339) — never bump this on a mere edit, only when
    you actually re-measured. --from-message marks the write as resolved from a
    relayed message; the server then forces method=relayed regardless of --method.

  thrum state get <kind>:<scope> [--agent AGENT]
    Read one state entry's value. --agent reads another agent's local-tier
    entries (fleet-tier entries are already shared).

  thrum state show <kind>:<scope> [--agent AGENT]
    Show one state entry with full metadata (method, as_of, established_by,
    freshness_owner, verify_cmd).

  thrum state list [--kind KIND] [--agent AGENT] [--json] [--quiet]
    List state entries (defaults to your own agent-local entries). Flags a
    STALE entry inline (past its kind's registered threshold, read live from
    `state describe` — never hardcoded) and, unless --quiet, emits a hint with
    the stale count. Use `--kind KIND` to spot duplicate/near-duplicate scope
    strings for the same entity (see the scope-consistency gotcha above).

  thrum state delete <kind>:<scope>
    Delete a state entry outright. On a fleet kind this writes a tombstone
    (peer-synced) rather than a bare local delete.

  thrum state describe <kind>
    Dump a declared kind's registry declaration (tier, staleness threshold,
    etc.) — the source `state list`'s staleness check reads from.

  thrum state history <kind>:<scope>
    Show the append-only write history for one entry (fleet kinds).

### Committed-Work Queue (per-agent, local-only)

  Per-agent list of the work an agent has committed to. One queue per agent_id;
  you EDIT your own, anyone may READ any queue. Local-only (never peer-synced),
  deleted when the agent is deleted. Distinct from beads (shared backlog of what
  COULD be done) and from the Tmux Command Queue above. A bundle is one unit of
  work; items are short checklist entries embedded inside a bundle (no nesting,
  no standalone items, no foreign keys). The title carries the whole content
  (there is no separate body field) and is capped at 40 KB at write time.
  Assignments and cross-agent status flow ONLY through messaging - no command
  writes another agent's queue. See the `thrum:using-the-queue` skill for the
  full lifecycle and assignment-handoff playbook.

  thrum queue add --title "..." [--from-message MSG_ID] [--ref TYPE:VALUE ...] [--priority N]
    Create a bundle in your own queue. At least one of --title / --from-message
    is required; explicit --title wins. The title may instead be the single
    quoted argument (`thrum queue add "..."`), but not both. --from-message lifts a received
    assignment in one command: message content becomes title, its author becomes
    assigned_by, its refs become refs (the message ID is then discarded, no
    stored link). --ref attaches a backlog reference (e.g. bead:thrum-abc12).

  thrum queue list [--status STATUS] [--agent AGENT_ID]
    List bundles in your queue, or another agent's with --agent (read is open to
    anyone). --status filters by pending / in_progress / blocked / done.

  thrum queue show BUNDLE_ID [--agent AGENT_ID]
    Show full detail (including embedded items) for one bundle.

  thrum queue start BUNDLE_ID
    Move a bundle to in_progress. Clears any block_reason.

  thrum queue block BUNDLE_ID [--reason "..."]
    Mark a bundle blocked, optionally recording a reason in block_reason.

  thrum queue done BUNDLE_ID
    Mark a bundle done. RESTING state - the bundle is kept, not deleted. Also
    clears any block_reason.

  thrum queue drop BUNDLE_ID
    Delete a bundle and every item inside it, regardless of status. The only
    destructive verb in the queue; not gated on items being closed first.

  thrum queue assign BUNDLE_ID AGENT_ID [AGENT_ID ...]
    Append agent IDs to a bundle's assigned_to routing metadata. Informational
    only - it does NOT write the named agent's queue and does not hand the work
    off.

  thrum queue item add BUNDLE_ID --title "..." [--from-message MSG_ID] [--ref TYPE:VALUE ...] [--priority N]
    Add one embedded item to an existing bundle.

  thrum queue item batch-add BUNDLE_ID --title "..." --title "..." ... [--ref TYPE:VALUE] [--priority N]
    Add several items in one call (repeated --title). --ref / --priority, if
    given, apply to every item in the batch.

  thrum queue item start | block | done BUNDLE_ID ITEM_ID
    Item-level status transitions (start / done clear the item's block_reason,
    same rule as the bundle level). Items have no drop and no rename; removal
    only ever happens at the bundle level via `thrum queue drop`.

### License

  thrum license
    Manage the Thrum license on this machine (activate / deactivate / status /
    oss-register subcommands; see `thrum license --help` for the current
    subcommand list). Nothing is sent without a yes; the daemon and its timers
    never send repository information. Interactive `thrum init` on an unlicensed
    machine asks [o] open source / [p] Pro / Enter Free. o registers this repo
    (git origin URL, repo ID, latest commit to my.thrum.team) after activation;
    p shows the activation link (activation is optional, sends machine ID and
    class); Enter sends nothing. `thrum license oss-register` registers on
    request and `thrum license activate` completes a recorded choice. The
    recorded choice is `.thrum/var/oss_register_consent` (delete to withdraw).
    The question is not asked with --no-daemon, --non-interactive, --quiet or a
    non-terminal stdin. `thrum daemon start` asks nothing. `thrum license
    activate --repo-origin/--repo-id` explicitly sends that origin/ID when
    activation starts.

### Free vs Pro

  Free: Terminal view.
  Pro: Terminal input, Conversation view, Memory Substrate, Peer Advanced
  Sharing, State Write, Queue Write, Dashboard Write, Email Bridge, Email
  Notify, Vault.
  A scoped OSS grant for a repository includes all Pro features, for that
  repository only; the web UI checks the daemon's own repository.
  Email: sending mail and changing email settings need Pro; reading email
  settings and status is Free. The email bridge starts only on a licensed
  machine. Vault: every `thrum vault` subcommand needs Pro. Telegram is Free.
  In the web UI, the State, Dashboard, Queue and Memory tabs show on Free only
  when they hold data (Memory: any memory at all). The CLI and agent messaging
  are not gated by tier.

### Profile

  thrum profile start | status | stop
    Daemon profile mode (CPU + heap + trace capture): start a capture, check
    status, stop and finalize.

### Provider

  thrum provider list
    List available provider templates.

  thrum provider show <name>
    Print a provider template's YAML.

  thrum provider eject <name>
    Copy a built-in provider template into .thrum/providers for local customization.

  thrum provider validate <path>
    Validate a standalone provider template file.

### Provision

  thrum provision <ssh-host>
    Provision a remote host as a Thrum agent over SSH.

  thrum tunnel <ssh-alias> --label <label> --remote-path <path> [--runtime <name> | --cli-only] [--role <role>] [--module <module>] [--worktrees-root <dir>] [--stealth] [--name <peer-name>]
    Pair with a remote Thrum daemon through an ssh config alias (key login only; MFA hosts are not supported yet)
    and register it as a peer. The alias comes from <thrum dir>/ssh/config (local, takes precedence) or ~/.ssh/config.
    --remote-path is the repo on the remote (absolute, ~, ~/rest or relative to its home); it must already be a git
    checkout and is never cloned. thrum is installed there from the local pro bundle when missing (GitHub release
    fallback), an uninitialised path is initialised non-interactively (the init flags --runtime, --role, --module,
    --worktrees-root, --stealth are forwarded only when given; --cli-only means init --runtime cli-only), and a
    stopped daemon is started. The EULA is accepted over the SSH path: every remote thrum command runs with
    THRUM_ACCEPT_EULA set to the EULA version bundled in the local binary.
