### Storage Maintenance

  thrum storage purge-weed [--repo <path>]... [--dry-run] [--json]
    One-time cleanup after the SeaweedFS removal. Stops leftover weed
    processes (same UID) and deletes ~/.thrum/var/seaweedfs and per-repo
    var/bin/weed, var/s3creds/, var/segments.db. Refuses (exit 2) while any
    live daemon is an old build or unreachable. Exit 0 purged/nothing to
    purge, 2 refused, 1 error.

### Vault (encrypted secrets)

  Scoped names: agent/<id>/<name> | role/<role>/<name> | project/<name>.
  Secrets are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) with a per-repository key
  under .thrum/var/tls/vault.key. Every verb supports --json.

  thrum vault set <name>
    Store or update a secret in the vault.

  thrum vault get <name>
    Retrieve a decrypted secret from the vault.

  thrum vault list [scope]
    List vault entries -- names, versions, sizes, timestamps (no values).

  thrum vault rm <name>
    Delete a secret and all its versions from the vault.

  thrum vault grant <agent> <name> --tier one-time|session|permanent [--session ID]
    Grant an agent access to a vault secret.

  thrum vault revoke <agent> <name>
    Revoke an agent's access to a vault secret.

  thrum vault grants [--agent NAME] [--secret NAME]
    List active grants for vault secrets.

  thrum vault capabilities
    Report vault backend capabilities.

  thrum vault audit
    List vault audit records (not yet implemented).

  thrum vault rotate-key
    Rotate the vault encryption key (not yet implemented).

  thrum vault backup [--out PATH]
    Back up all vault secrets into a passphrase-protected bundle.

  thrum vault restore --from <bundle> [--name NAME] [--force]
    Restore vault secrets from a passphrase-protected bundle.

### Blob (encrypted binary objects)

  Scoped names: agent/<id>/<name> | role/<role>/<name> | project/<name>.
  Same encryption/key as the vault, for larger binary objects. Every verb
  supports --json.

  thrum blob put <name> [--file PATH | --stdin]
    Store or update a binary object in the blob store.

  thrum blob get <name> [--output PATH]
    Retrieve a blob by writing to a file -- prints path (no bytes on stdout).

  thrum blob cat <name> [--cap BYTES]
    Print blob contents to stdout (default cap: 1 MiB; use --cap or
    'blob get --output' for larger blobs).

  thrum blob list [scope]
    List blob objects -- names, versions, sizes, timestamps (no contents).

  thrum blob rm <name>
    Delete a blob object and all its versions.

  thrum blob grant <agent> <name> --tier one-time|session|permanent [--session ID]
    Grant an agent access to a blob object.

  thrum blob revoke <agent> <name>
    Revoke an agent's access to a blob object.

  thrum blob grants [--agent NAME] [--secret NAME]
    List active grants for blob objects.

  thrum blob capabilities
    Report blob backend capabilities.

  thrum blob audit
    List blob audit records (not yet implemented).

### Watcher (deterministic code/issue watcher)

  thrum watcher scan
    Preview the deterministic findings-needing-triage as JSON (read-only).

  thrum watcher emit
    Run the full cycle and apply findings via the sink (writes store + optional beads).

  thrum watcher report
    Render the last run's md+json artifact (and optional digest).

  thrum watcher mirror
    Refresh the bead snapshot cache (standalone, deletion-safe).

  thrum watcher rebuild [--cold]
    Rebuild the SQLite projection (Tier-1 from JSONL; Tier-2 cold re-scan with --cold).

### Detect (pane-content detection engine)

  The single match engine both the daemon and the bash supervisor sweep
  route through for pane-content detection, backed by the embedded
  detection registry. One of --schema-hash, --pattern, or --category
  is required.

  thrum detect --schema-hash
    Print the embedded registry's schema hash (sha256 of the raw bytes) and exit.

  thrum detect --pattern '<RE2 regex>' --pane-file <f>
    Ad-hoc RE2 pattern match against --pane-file, bypassing the registry.

  thrum detect --category <name> --pane-file <f> [--runtime NAME] [--runtime-version V]
    Evaluate a registry category against the pane; --runtime picks the
    single version-appropriate entry, otherwise every entry in the category
    is tried and the first match wins.
    Exit 0 + matched entry name (or custom_message) on match; exit 1
    (silent) on no match.

### Graph Substrate

  thrum graph backfill
    Migrate all memory_record rows to the graph substrate (idempotent, one-shot).

  thrum graph import-from-bd
    Import a bd JSONL export into the graph substrate (idempotent).

  thrum graph export-beads-jsonl
    Write graph issues as a bd JSONL export file (read-only).

### Hook Audit Log (hooklog)

  thrum hooklog capture
    Read one PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook payload from stdin and append it to
    the hook audit log. Captures every tool call, not just thrum invocations.

  thrum hooklog detect
    Report PreToolUse/PostToolUse correlation orphans found in the hook audit log.

  thrum hooklog guard
    Read one PreToolUse hook payload from stdin and BLOCK a thrum/bd Bash
    command with an unsafe backtick.

### Log Inspection

  thrum log search <logname> <query> [--ignore-case|-i] [--limit|-n N]
    Brute-force scan a log's CURRENT-DAY file (older history is in the .gz
    rotations). --ignore-case for a case-insensitive match; --limit caps
    matches (0 = all).

### Agent Status

  thrum agent status
    Show your own agent status (identity, context %, memory counts).

  thrum agent status <name>
    Reconcile the named agent on its home daemon and show the result
    (changed or no-change, phase before/after, home daemon, changed decision
    fields). This writes: it refreshes the agent's decision state.

### Daemon

  On macOS, after installing or updating the binary, run `thrum daemon launchd install`
  from the project to run and restart the daemon as your user’s launchd agent.
  A daemon started from a terminal or agent pane inherits that terminal’s Local Network permission and can lose LAN peers; do not use the old cron script.
  Check `launchctl list | grep com.leonletto.thrum.daemon` for the per-repo job and PID, run `thrum daemon status`, and confirm peers reconnect.

  thrum daemon start [--no-git-sync]
    Start daemon in background. --no-git-sync disables remote git sync
    (daemon.sync_via_git=false). --local is a deprecated alias, kept for
    one release.
    G2 guard: refuses non-git CWD; --force bypasses.

  thrum daemon stop
    Stop daemon gracefully.

  thrum daemon status
    Show daemon running state, PID, uptime, version.
    Prints one git-sync line: "Git sync: not used (network sync)" or "Git sync (a-sync): ON — pushing to origin/a-sync (last push <t> / last error <e>)" (never/none when unset); it is the daemon's boot-resolved gate, not config.
    Shows Identity block: daemon_id, repo_name, hostname, repo_path, git_origin_url, init_at.

  thrum daemon restart
    Stop and restart daemon.

  thrum daemon logs [--follow|-f] [--lines|-n N] [--since DURATION|DATE]  # v0.8.0
    View the daemon log file (.thrum/var/log/daemon.log). Default: last 50 lines.
    --follow streams new lines; --lines N shows N lines (0 = all);
    --since filters by time (e.g., "1h", "7d", "2026-04-09", RFC 3339).
    Daemon uses lumberjack rotation: 10 MB max, 4 backups, 28 days, gzip.
    Log level controlled by `daemon.log_level` in config.json.

  thrum daemon repair-lane-messages [--apply] [--ids-out PATH] [--job JOB_ID] [--timeout DUR] [--json]
    One-shot lane-side repair of the "ambiguous tie" message ids the
    backup messages gate reports. RPC to a RUNNING daemon (lane.repair_messages.start/
    status): starts a background job and polls it (plan ~2 min, apply ~3 min for ~35k ids).
    Default is a DRY RUN that only plans. --apply appends the SQL-derived row as the last
    line of each id's lane file through the daemon's own lane writer (zero SQL writes);
    a second --apply writes 0. --apply is refused when git sync is on (config key
    sync_via_git), when a sync cycle is in flight, or when
    the caller is not an operator/human. --ids-out copies the uncapped id list;
    --job re-attaches to a job. Leave buckets (non-tie branches, SQL rows missing key
    columns, zero created_at) are reported and never written, so the backup gate is
    expected to still report converged=false for those ids after --apply.

## Common Agent Workflows

### Start working on a repo

  thrum init
  thrum daemon start
  thrum worktree create <agent-name>
  cd <worktree-path>   # path printed by worktree create ("Worktree created at <path>")
  thrum quickstart --name <agent-name> --role implementer --module auth --intent "Building auth flow"

Quickstart must run inside the agent's worktree: the main repo refuses new-agent binds.

### Send a message to a teammate

  echo 'Auth module ready for review' | thrum send --to @reviewer --scope module:auth -

### Send to multiple explicit recipients

  echo 'Stopping for lunch, back in 30' | thrum send --to @alice --to @bob -

  Note: --broadcast and @everyone were removed by design;
  do not restore them. There is no team-wide broadcast — name
  every recipient explicitly with repeatable --to.

### Check inbox and reply

  thrum inbox --unread
  thrum sent --unread
  echo 'Looks good, merging now' | thrum reply msg_01HXE... -

### Coordinate on shared files

  thrum who-has auth.go
  thrum team --compact

### Check team status

  thrum team

### Check if an agent is online

  thrum ping @reviewer

### Get a combined status overview

  thrum overview

### Cross-repo peer communication (Tailscale, v0.7.0)

  Host mode (default): when the Tailscale app is installed thrum binds the
  host's 100.64.0.0/10 IP directly (no var/tsnet directory). A single IP is
  advertised in the peercode. Daemon env: THRUM_TS_AUTHKEY must be in the
  daemon's env (via .thrum/.env); 'thrum daemon restart' does not re-source
  .env — re-export or restart via launchd/systemd so the daemon sees it.
  Multi-tailnet hosts must pin the reachable tailnet with THRUM_PEER_LISTEN_IP
  (alias THRUM_TS_LISTEN_IP); verify with 'thrum daemon status' + 'tailscale
  status' (LocalAPI may see a different tailnet than net.InterfaceAddrs).
  Preflight from the JOINER before pairing: nc -z <advertised-ip> <port>.

  # Machine A (adder — listener; requires --label in non-interactive shells)
  thrum peer add --type tailscale --label alice   # Displays 16-digit peercode, blocks 5min
  # Machine B (joiner — dialer; peercode carries destination, no --addr for tailscale)
  thrum peer join --type tailscale --peercode alice:100.64.1.5:44123:7392168401234567
  # Both daemons now route messages bidirectionally

  # Configure proxy agents so remote agents are addressable locally
  thrum peer configure alice add-agent planner
  echo 'Ready for review' | thrum send --to @alice:planner -

### Launch agents in tmux sessions (v0.7.1+)

  # Create a worktree, register the agent, and create the tmux session in one step (v0.8.2)
  # The agent is NOT running yet — tmux launch starts the runtime.
  thrum worktree create api-feature -b feature/api-refactor \
    --name impl_api --role implementer --module api
  thrum tmux launch api-feature

  # OR for an existing worktree: create the session + run quickstart in one command
  thrum tmux create implementer-api \
    --cwd ~/.workspaces/myproj/api-feature \
    --name impl_api --role implementer --module api --runtime claude
  thrum tmux launch implementer-api
  # quickstart runs automatically inside the pane during create; tmux launch
  # then starts the runtime. Hard-errors if the session was created with
  # --no-agent or the worktree has no identity file.

  echo 'Your epic is thrum-abc. Start working.' | thrum send --to @impl_api -

  # Check session status
  thrum tmux status

  # Dispatch a command to the agent's pane and await completion (v0.8.0)
  thrum tmux queue implementer-api "make test" --wait --timeout 300

  # Restart an agent with context preserved (graceful by default in v0.8.0)
  thrum tmux restart implementer-api
  thrum tmux restart implementer-api --force       # Skip graceful save, extract JSONL directly

### Orchestrator workflow (v0.8.0)

  The orchestrator role executes plans epic-by-epic with review gates. It creates
  worktrees, launches implementers, dispatches tasks via tmux queue, manages
  agent lifecycle, and hands back a merge report. See the `thrum:orchestrate`
  skill for the full playbook.

  # Configure worktrees base path (affects `thrum worktree create`)
  # Edit .thrum/config.json:
  #   "worktrees": { "base_path": "/abs/path/to/worktrees", "beads_enabled": true, "thrum_enabled": true }
  #   "orchestration": { "merge_target": "main", "default_autonomy": "end_only" }

### Recover context

  thrum state set --kind personal_state --scope <scope> --value '<json>'   # Personal state
  thrum queue list                                                          # Committed work
  thrum prime                  # Restart snapshot and session state, delivered at session start

## Key Concepts

  Agent       An AI agent or human identified by role + module. ID: agent:role:hash.
  Session     A work period for an agent. Tracks scopes, refs, heartbeats.
  Role        Agent's function (e.g., implementer, reviewer, planner).
  Module      Component the agent is responsible for (e.g., auth, db, ui).
  Scope       Routing metadata on messages (format: type:value, e.g., module:auth).
  Ref         Reference metadata (format: type:value, e.g., pr:42, mention:reviewer).
  Mention     Tag an explicit agent: @agent_name. Stored as ref type "mention".
              Bare role names that are not also an agent ID resolve to nobody
              (role-based fan-out was removed by design).
  Sync        The `a-sync` orphan branch accessed via `.git/thrum-sync/a-sync` worktree.
  Heartbeat   Periodic signal from agent. Extracts git state, updates last-seen.
  Context     Restart snapshots, personal state, and queue bundles that carry work across compaction or session boundaries.
  Peer        A Tailscale-connected remote daemon for direct machine-to-machine sync.
  Runtime     AI coding tool preset (Claude, Codex, Cursor, etc.) with config defaults.
  Monitor     A long-running child process whose stdout/stderr is watched by the daemon.
              Regex matches emit synthetic Thrum messages to a target agent. Local-only.

## MCP Server

  thrum mcp serve [--agent-id NAME]
    Start MCP stdio server for native agent messaging (JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout).
    Use --agent-id to select identity file. Configure in .claude/settings.json.

  MCP Tools:
    send_message(to, content, reply_to?, metadata?)
      Send a message to another agent via to=@agent_name.
      - to: recipient @agent_name, explicit only (required)
      - content: message text (required)
      - reply_to: message ID to reply to (optional)
      - metadata: optional key-value pairs (optional)

    check_messages(limit?)
      Poll for unread messages mentioning this agent; does not mark them read.
      - limit: max messages to return (optional, default: 50)

    wait_for_message(timeout?)
      Block until a message arrives (WebSocket push) or timeout.
      - timeout: max seconds to wait (optional, default: 300, max: 600)

    list_agents(include_offline?)
      List registered agents with active/offline status.
      - include_offline: include inactive agents (optional, default: true)

    broadcast_message: REMOVED. @everyone
      fan-out was removed by design and this tool had no valid replacement
      once that syntax was gone — do not restore it. Use send_message with
      an explicit @agent_name recipient instead.

## Daemon

  Socket:     .thrum/var/thrum.sock (Unix socket, JSON-RPC 2.0)
  WebSocket:  ws://localhost:<port>/ (auto-assigned and reused on restart when available; see `thrum daemon status`)
  PID file:   .thrum/var/thrum.pid (JSON format: PID, RepoPath, StartedAt, SocketPath)
  Port file:  .thrum/var/ws.port (actual WebSocket port)
  Lock:       Socket flock for SIGKILL resilience (auto-released on process death)

  Start:      thrum daemon start (pre-startup duplicate detection via repo affinity)
  Stop:       thrum daemon stop
  Health:     thrum daemon status (shows mode/interface/provenance, advertised peer IP:port, other candidate CGNAT IPs, ambiguity warning; reachability is UNVERIFIED until the joiner proves it with nc -z)

## Environment Variables

  THRUM_NAME          Agent name (highest priority for identity file selection)
  THRUM_ROLE          Agent role (overrides identity file)
  THRUM_MODULE        Agent module (overrides identity file)
  THRUM_DISPLAY       Display name (overrides identity file)
  THRUM_NO_GIT_SYNC   Disable remote git (a-)sync (daemon.sync_via_git=false) -- set to "1"
  THRUM_LOCAL         Deprecated alias for THRUM_NO_GIT_SYNC, kept one release -- set to "1"
  THRUM_WS_PORT       WebSocket port (default: auto)
  THRUM_HOME          Pin repo path for all commands (set by thrum-startup.sh)
  THRUM_AGENT_ID      Pin caller identity for daemon RPC
  THRUM_SOCKET        Unix socket path override
  THRUM_TS_AUTHKEY    Tailscale auth key for peering (must be in the DAEMON's env via .thrum/.env; 'thrum daemon restart' does not re-source .env)
  THRUM_TS_PORT       Tailscale listener port (default: auto). Setting it alone does not start the Tailscale listener; it also needs tailscale.listen=true, THRUM_TS_LISTENER=true, or an existing tailscale peer.
  THRUM_TS_HOSTNAME   tsnet hostname override (tsnet mode only)
  THRUM_TS_STATE_DIR  tsnet state directory (tsnet mode only)
  THRUM_PEER_LISTEN_IP  Pin the advertised Tailscale host-IP (100.64.0.0/10) on multi-tailnet hosts; must be a local CGNAT IP (alias: THRUM_TS_LISTEN_IP). Validate with 'thrum daemon status' + 'tailscale status'; preflight with 'nc -z <ip> <port>' from the joiner.
  THRUM_TS_LISTEN_IP  Alias for THRUM_PEER_LISTEN_IP (same validation)
  THRUM_TS_LISTENER   Tailscale peer listener switch: true/1/yes/on or false/0/no/off (exact, lowercase; anything else fails daemon boot loudly; empty = unset). Overrides config.json tailscale.listen (precedence: env > config > unset). Unset means OFF by default, but the listener stays on automatically when the box already has paired tailscale peers; explicit false wins over existing peers. Must be in the DAEMON's env (e.g. via .thrum/.env) when the daemon starts; restart the daemon after changing it.
  THRUM_LAN_LISTENER  LAN peer listener switch (--type network): same values and precedence as THRUM_TS_LISTENER, overriding config.json lan.listen. Unset means OFF by default, but the listener stays on when the box already has network peers or persisted LAN listener endpoints; explicit false wins.
  THRUM_TS_MODE       Tailscale mode: host (default, binds host IP) or embedded (tsnet virtual interface; state in var/tsnet). Overrides config.json tailscale.mode (precedence: env > config > host). Dev, sandbox and lab daemons default to embedded so they bind no tailnet-reachable listener; export THRUM_TS_MODE=host before launching to opt in. THRUM_TS_ENABLED is deprecated and ignored — Tailscale auto-starts when peers are configured (THRUM_TS_ENABLED previously logged a deprecation warning only).
  THRUM_NO_HINTS=1    Suppress CLI hints (Shape B stderr trailers). Truthy: any non-empty value except "0" or "false". Also suppressed by --quiet and --json.
  THRUM_NO_REMINDERS=1   Suppress reinforcement (reminder) CLI hints only — kind=reinforcement — from BOTH stderr and JSON. Detection hints still fire. Truthy: any non-empty value except 0 or false.
  THRUM_ACCEPT_EULA=<version>  Accept the bundled end-user licence (EULA) without a prompt. Must equal the bundled version exactly (the version the licence notice prints); 1, yes, true or any other value does not count. Required for non-interactive runs (CI, scripts, agents, daemon services) before any command except help, version and completion will run. The EULA is also shown on the first interactive run; typing yes accepts it. Acceptance is recorded locally, once per bundled text, in ~/.thrum/license/eula-acceptance-<version>-<sha12>.json (a new version adds a file and leaves the old one; a corrupt record at the exact path is moved aside to a sibling `<name>.invalid-*` file, never overwritten). A matching THRUM_ACCEPT_EULA is accepted even where HOME is unset; the record is then kept only if the store can be written. Agent panes, monitor jobs and scheduled commands the daemon starts receive THRUM_ACCEPT_EULA and THRUM_LICENSE_DIR, so they find the same record. The gate makes no network call.

## Licence Acceptance

  The first run of any thrum command (except help, version and completion) checks
  the acceptance record for the bundled EULA version. Without a matching record,
  an interactive terminal shows the title, version, sha256, URL and a one-line
  summary, and asks you to type yes. A non-interactive run exits with
  "thrum: EULA not accepted" and prints the URL and the exact variable to set. A new
  EULA version, or a changed sha256 for the same version, asks again.

## Git Sync (a-sync) On/Off

  daemon.sync_via_git (positive-form, current) controls whether the sync loop
  pushes/fetches over git at all: sync_via_git=false disables all git
  push/fetch in the sync loop (git a-sync off; peer/network sync via
  daemon.sync.enabled is unaffected). Use for public repos where you don't
  want to expose agent messages to origin, or for a daemon that only has
  network (peer) sync configured.

  thrum daemon start --no-git-sync       # Via CLI flag (current)
  THRUM_NO_GIT_SYNC=1 thrum daemon start # Via environment variable (current)
  thrum daemon start --local             # Deprecated alias, kept one release
  THRUM_LOCAL=1 thrum daemon start       # Deprecated alias, kept one release

  Persists in .thrum/config.json: { "daemon": { "sync_via_git": false } }
  (the legacy { "daemon": { "local_only": true } } key is still read and
  folded into sync_via_git on load for one release — see the Configuration
  Reference below — but new writes use sync_via_git.)
  Priority: CLI flag > env var > config file > default. The default is OFF:
  git sync is opt-in. With no sync_via_git key and no sync stanza, git sync
  is off; local_only=false (or absent) no longer implies on. Enable it with
  "sync_via_git": true or a sync stanza with an a-sync mechanism. thrum init
  leaves sync_via_git unset (resolves OFF; no explicit false is written), even
  when it attaches to an existing origin/a-sync. sync_via_git replicates
  fleet-wide once explicitly set; the sync stanza is local-only.
  Check status: thrum sync status (shows "Mode: git sync disabled
  (daemon.sync_via_git=false)" or "Mode: normal"; the underlying sync_state
  enum value stays the frozen literal "local-only" for one release,
  cross-version compatibility)

## Configuration Reference (.thrum/config.json)

  Full schema for .thrum/config.json. Most fields are optional — omit a block
  to use defaults. View the effective configuration with `thrum config show`.

  {
    "runtime": {
      "primary": "claude"                   // a runtime preset name; see "thrum runtime list"
    },
    "daemon": {
      "sync_via_git": false,                 // disable remote git (a-)sync (current key)
      "local_only": true,                    // deprecated alias for !sync_via_git, kept one release
      "sync_interval": 60,                   // seconds between syncs (default 60)
      "ws_port": "auto",                     // "auto" or a specific fixed port like "9999"
      "peer_port": "auto",                   // Tailscale listener port
      "single_agent_mode": true,             // skip messaging infrastructure
      "log_level": "info"                    // v0.8.0: debug | info | warn | error (default: info)
    },
    "peers": {
      "auto_connect": true,                  // auto-connect to known peers on daemon start
      "pairing_code_length": 16              // length of generated pairing codes
    },
    "worktrees": {                           // v0.8.0: used by `thrum worktree create/teardown`
      "base_path": "~/.thrum/worktrees/myproj",   // absolute path where new worktrees are created
      "beads_enabled": true,                 // init default (bd on PATH); does not gate .beads/redirect
      "thrum_enabled": true                  // create .thrum/redirect + identities/ in new worktrees
    },
    "orchestration": {                       // v0.8.0: used by the orchestrator role
      "merge_target": "main",                // branch for final merge after all epics complete
      "default_autonomy": "end_only"         // "per_epic" (approve each epic) | "end_only"
    },
    "restart": {
      "max_lines": 200,                      // max transcript lines for agent resurrect (default 200)
      "auto_threshold": 0,                   // 0-100 context % trigger for auto-restart; 0 = off
      "graceful_timeout": 300                 // seconds to wait for graceful snapshot save
    },
    "backup": {
      "dir": ".thrum/backup",                // backup directory (relative or absolute)
      "schedule": "24h",                     // Go duration format; omit or set to "off" to disable
      "retention": {
        "daily": 5,                          // -1 keeps all; 0 keeps none
        "weekly": 4,
        "monthly": -1
      },
      "post_backup": "",                     // shell command to run after each backup
      "plugins": []                          // third-party backup plugin definitions
    },
    "identity_guard": {                      // v0.9.0: named enforcement checkpoints; 3 modes each
      "cross_worktree": "strict",            // PID from wrong worktree
      "quickstart_self_rename": "strict",    // caller re-registering under new name
      "quickstart_name_collision": "strict", // requested name held by live foreign PID
      "non_git_bootstrap": "strict",         // thrum init / daemon start outside git repo
      "unauthenticated_rpc": "strict",       // mutating RPC with no resolvable identity
      "daemon_writer_liveness": "strict",    // daemon writing to dead agent's identity file
      "prime_ownership": "strict",           // thrum prime called from sub-agent
      "dead_pid_auto_reclaim": "warn"        // informational; dead PID reclaimed automatically
    }
    // Modes: "strict" (hard error) | "warn" (log + allow) | "off" (skip)
    // unauthenticated_rpc/identity_mismatch (forgery) ignores mode config.
    // Narrow exception (v0.9.0): shared-worktree claim trust. If peercred picks agent Y but
    // client claims X, and X is also registered in the peercred-resolved worktree
    // (state.IsAgentInWorktree), the claim is honored. Cross-worktree claims still fail.
    // Runtime override (no repo commit): .thrum/var/guard-daemon.json (same keys; daemon-level wins).
    // v0.9.1: anonymous-caller rejection scoped to PROVABLY anonymous
    // callers only (git-root-missing or no-worktree-match). Peercred introspection
    // failures (kernel peer-creds or gopsutil.Cwd errored) fall through to legacy
    // client-asserted identity — the server never treats them as anonymous. slog.Warn
    // at step=pid failed / step=cwd failed is the diagnostic path.
  }

  Config key for worktree base directory: `worktrees.base_path` (NOT `worktree_dir`).

## Beads + Thrum Integration

  Beads (task tracking) and Thrum (messaging) together provide complete agent
  memory and coordination:

  Beads: what agents were doing -- tasks, status, dependencies, context recovery
  Thrum: what agents said -- messages, presence, notifications, session tracking

  Both use Git as persistence layer. State survives session boundaries,
  context compaction, and machine changes.

## Identity Resolution Order

  File selection (which .thrum/identities/*.json gets loaded):
  1. THRUM_NAME env var → load {name}.json directly
  2. Solo-agent auto-select → only one .json file exists
  3. PID match (v0.7.0) → walk process tree to find runtime PID, match `agent_pid` field
     (v0.8.0 renamed `claude_pid` to `agent_pid` for multi-runtime support)
  4. Worktree match (v0.7.0) → filter by current git worktree name
  5. Error if no unambiguous selection

  Field value overrides (after file is loaded):
  CLI flags (--role, --module) > env vars (THRUM_ROLE, THRUM_MODULE) > identity file

  Note: THRUM_NAME env var takes highest priority for file selection,
  overriding even the --name CLI flag.

  Identity file format (v5, since v0.8.0):
  {
    "version": 5,
    "repo_id": "r_...",
    "agent": { "name": "...", "role": "...", "module": "...", "display": "..." },
    "worktree": "main",
    "agent_pid": 12345,              // v0.8.0 (renamed from claude_pid)
    "preferred_runtime": "claude",   // v0.8.0: set by `thrum quickstart --runtime`
    "runtime": "claude",             // v0.7.1: auto-detected runtime
    "tmux_session": "name:0.0",      // v0.7.1
    "agent_status": "working",       // v0.8.0: working | idle | blocked
    "agent_status_updated_at": "...",// v0.8.0
    "updated_at": "..."
  }

  `thrum prime` refreshes `tmux_session`, `preferred_runtime`, and `branch` on
  every run — matters when agents relaunch under a different runtime or move
  between branches.
